questions: Do you send messages to your friends? Who do you message the most?
After you hit the send button, what do you think happens to the message before it reaches your friend?
What did you write, and why did you choose those words?
When you send a message that’s really important—like planning a surprise or sharing good news—how do you decide what to write, and what do you hope your friend will feel when they read it?
Can you think of a time when a message arrived at a very important moment, like when you needed help or when something big happened?
What would you write, and why would you think those words would help you in the future?
If you could change one thing about the message that helped your brother find the station, what would you change and why?
What is one benefit of gene editing that supporters mention?
Why do critics worry about changes made to an embryo?
What do supporters say is the difference between treating a disease and improving a trait like height?
How do you think families who can’t afford these enhancements might feel about fairness and inequality?
Why do you think fairness matters to families who can’t afford new treatments, especially when those treatments might give children an advantage?
Should gene editing be allowed to treat serious diseases?
If a country only allowed gene editing for serious diseases, how would they enforce those rules to stop non‑therapeutic edits, and what challenges might that enforcement face?
